questions.question: You need to identify which network security group rule blocks inbound TCP 443 traffic from a specific internet IP address to VM1. Which Azure Network Watcher tool should you use?

options.why: Correct. It tests one flow and returns the rule that allows or denies it.
Next hop shows routing, not security rules.
Packet capture records traffic but does not name the NSG rule.
VPN troubleshoot diagnoses VPN gateways and connections.

questions.explanation: IP flow verify checks a specific protocol, local and remote IP address and port against the effective security rules.

questions.question: VM1 in Spoke1 cannot connect to VM2 in Spoke2. Both spokes are peered with a hub. Next hop for traffic from VM1 to VM2 returns None. What is the cause?

options.text: There is no route from Spoke1 to Spoke2 because virtual network peering is not transitive
options.why: Correct. Next hop None means the packet is dropped.

options.text: An NSG on the VM2 subnet denies the traffic
options.why: An NSG would not change the next hop result.

options.text: IP forwarding is disabled on VM1
options.why: IP forwarding is needed on appliances that forward traffic, not on the source VM.

options.text: The private DNS zone is not linked to Spoke1
options.why: DNS does not affect the next hop for an IP address.

questions.explanation: Spokes that are peered only with a hub do not have routes to each other. Peer them directly or use user-defined routes to an NVA in the hub.

questions.question: You need to test whether VM1 can connect to sql1.contoso.com on TCP 1433, and if it cannot, identify the hop where the connection fails. Which tool should you use?

options.why: Correct. It tests end-to-end connectivity to a VM, IP address or FQDN on a port and reports the failing hop.
IP flow verify evaluates NSG rules for one flow and does not test the full path.
Effective routes show routing but do not test connectivity.
Flow logs record traffic over time.

questions.explanation: Connection troubleshoot (az network watcher test-connectivity) reports reachability, latency and issues such as NSG rules or routes on each hop.

questions.question: Traffic from Subnet1 is routed to a network virtual appliance (NVA) by a user-defined route. Connection troubleshoot reports that traffic stops at the NVA. Which two configurations should you verify? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: IP forwarding is enabled on the network interface of the NVA
options.why: Correct. Without it, Azure drops packets that are not addressed to the NVA.

options.text: A return route through the NVA exists for the destination subnet
options.why: Correct. Asymmetric routing causes stateful appliances to drop traffic.

options.text: A service endpoint is enabled on Subnet1
options.why: Service endpoints apply to Azure PaaS services.

options.text: The NVA has a public IP address
options.why: Forwarding between private subnets does not require a public IP address.

questions.explanation: NVAs need IP forwarding, and traffic must return through the same appliance.

questions.question: You need to view all the routes, including system routes and user-defined routes, that apply to the network interface of VM1, and see which routes are not active. What should you use?

options.text: Effective routes on the network interface
options.why: Correct. It lists every route source, prefix, next hop and state, including Invalid routes.
A route table shows only its own user-defined routes.
Effective security rules show NSG rules.
Connection monitor tests connectivity over time.

questions.explanation: Effective routes (az network nic show-effective-route-table) combine system, BGP and user-defined routes and show their state.
